text:
oliver: Heads-up — after the kernel swap to kernel-quant-v2 (rolled 03:10 UTC) we're seeing a tail latency regression on mixtral-moerouter for long sequences (seq > 1024). p50 stable, p95 +12%, p99 +18% on prod-dedicated. Any obvious suspects?

anya: saw the alert stream. queuing traces now, will attach flamegraphs. :eyes:

profiling-bot: Flamegraph + raw traces uploaded: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/profiles/1945674321/flame.tar.gz (profile span: 03:05-03:40 UTC)

sam: quick pass over the flame shows kernel_softmax_hot path time jumped and KV cache miss rate spiked. sample metrics from traces: 
```
kv_cache.misses_pct 23.1
kernel.softmax_ms 4.8 (was ~1.1)	router.topk_latency_pct +13
```
looks like more cache thrashing for long prefixes.

lee: possible explanation: the new packing heuristic that shipped with the kernel swap packs larger long-seq batches more aggressively, which can amplify cache eviction for MoE. can we re-run with packing.max_tokens lowered? also we should try a quick rollback to confirm kernel is the main cause.

zhang: another angle — router logits temp was nudged last week (temp=1.05 -> 1.2) which widens logits and increases topk dispersion. that + tighter packing could push requests to different experts and blow the expert KV hit locality. propose: temporarily set router.top_k=16 (was 32) and router.logit_temp=1.0 for a canary.

oliver: plan proposal: two parallel canaries for 2h: (A) rollback kernel -> kernel-quant-v1 on 10% traffic; (B) keep kernel-quant-v2 but set top_k=16+logit_temp=1.0 on another 10%. collect p95/p99 + kv_miss + expert-imbalance. @lee take A, @anya take B for tracing.

lee: taking A, starting rollback canary now (10% traffic). will post deploy id.

dev-bot: Deploy started: rollback/kernel-quant-v1 -> canary-id: cb4f7a. Traffic split: 10% rollback, 10% topk-canary, 80% prod.

profiling-bot: Canary traces for both groups streaming to https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/profiles/1945674321/canaries/ (will be available after 15m)

sam: quick numbers after 30m into canary: rollback group p99 dropped from 210ms -> 182ms, kv_cache.miss_pct -> 6.7 (was 23.1). topk-canary group (kernel-quant-v2 + top_k=16) p99 -> 190ms, kv_miss_pct -> 9.8. baseline prod still at p99 210ms.

anya: trace diff shows in rollback group the kernel.softmax_hot path shrinks and we regain longer-lived KV entries (prefix evictions down). in topk-canary we also see much better expert locality compared to prod. attaching short diff snippet: 
```
# rollback vs prod (p99 component ms)
kv_lookup: 24 -> 8
softmax: 62 -> 28
router_select: 12 -> 10

# topk-canary vs prod
kv_lookup: 24 -> 11
router_select: 12 -> 9
```

zhang: good signal — both knobs help, but kernel rollback gives biggest win. suggests kernel change introduced a hot softmax kernel path regression + interacted poorly with packing. we should file a kernel regression bug and ask kernel team to bisect the quant / vectorized softmax change.

oliver: agreed. immediate action items: 
- lee: keep rollback canary for 2h, then scale rollback to 30% if stable.
- anya: collect full canary traces and generate delta flamegraphs (p95/p99 breakdown).
- zhang/sam: open kernel regression ticket with perf traces + sample workloads; add packing heuristic as possible interaction.
- infra: add short-lived metric: expert_kv_hit_ratio per-expert to make future regressions easier.

lee: started scaling rollback to 30% now (monitoring for errors).

sam: FYI, quick mitigation we can push without kernel change: reduce batch.packing.max_tokens and lower router.top_k to 16 globally as short-term relief, but that may impact throughput — tradeoff noted.

oliver: let's track tradeoffs in the incident doc. good work everyone. next sync in #eng-runtime in 30m. :thumbsup:
